statement: Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee.
rule: A tuple (React adapter, exact React, Pixi adapter, exact pixi.js) is verified on a render backend when its cell passed on that backend in this record (every command, every conformance scenario and the render check) and every boundary probe and every negative case of this record behaved as expected. A run on the expected-blank-render list (adapterMatrix.expectedBlankRender) that failed exactly as listed is not a failure, but verifies nothing. Each tuple lists every backend it is verified on; backends are never inferred from each other.

rendering.note: Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence.

environment.os: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (container in a Firecracker microVM)
environment.cpu: 4 vCPU Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 15 GiB RAM
environment.gpu: none: no GPU device in the machine (/dev/dri absent); every backend renders in software

backends.webgl: WebGL 2.0 through ANGLE on SwiftShader: 'ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)'; flags --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader
backends.webgpu: Dawn on SwiftShader's Vulkan device: adapter vendor 'google', architecture 'swiftshader', isFallbackAdapter true (a software fallback adapter); flags as WebGL plus --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader. Without those flags headless Chromium exposes navigator.gpu (secure contexts) but requestAdapter() returns null

commands: node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --tier nightly --patches all --cell <a third of the cells> --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs   (three shards in parallel)
notes: Tier: nightly with `--patches all` (297 cells: every React adapter, React 18.0 to 19.3, at its minimum and latest audited patch x the newest audited patch of every Pixi 8 minor and pixi.js 7.2.0, 7.2.4, 7.3.0, 7.3.3, 7.4.2 and 7.4.3), a superset of the scheduled nightly tier's 216 cells. Render backends: WebGL and WebGPU (`adapterMatrix.tiers.nightly.renderers`); Pixi 7 cells WebGL only.

Second full record of this machine and software profile on 2026-10-10 (`--sequence 2`): it supersedes the first 2026-10-10 record, whose 184 cells ran before the React 18 minors became packages (react-18.0 to react-18.3, the old react-18 renamed react-18.3) and before the Pixi 7 adapter covered 7.2 and 7.3. Only the newest record of a machine and GPU profile counts, so verifiedRanges derive from this record (plus other machines' records).

Commit 83aa8a8 on claude/react18-minors-pixi7-widen. Fresh: a new work directory, packages rebuilt with `pnpm build --force`, tarballs packed from that build, `--no-cache` (no verdict reused), CI=true. The npm download cache was shared (registry tarballs are integrity-checked).

Three cell shards ran in parallel on 4 vCPUs with the probes (cells 16:24 to 17:23 UTC, 59 minutes; about 35 s per cell per shard), then the negative cases and the data-only probes. No test timed out and no failure was retried.

Cells with React 18.0.0, 18.1.0 and 18.2.0 ran with harness/test/lend-act.ts, which lends React the act of react-dom/test-utils (React exports act from 18.3.0 on); the adapters and every check are unchanged. Pixi 7.2 cells compiled the Pixi 7 type consumer without the pixi8-names-rejected assertions (adapterMatrix typeAssertions, from 7.3.0), recorded in each cell.json.

Commits after this one change documentation, generated tables, the verification tooling and comments only; `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs compare --record 2026-10-10.2 --tarballs <fresh pack>` shows whether a later commit packs the same code (Markdown and build logs aside).

@pixi-react-provisional/react-18.0 supports React 18.0.x (tested: 18.0.0), but React 18.3.1 is installed. Install and use the adapter package that matches the installed React minor (for example @pixi-react-provisional/react-18.3).

dataOnly.statement: Data only, not verified: these results are never verification, never enter verifiedRanges and never change a peer range.
dataOnly.description: Data-only probes (issue 17). Each probe installs the packed adapters beside a React or pixi.js the adapter does not declare, ignoring peers, and records what every cell command does. The adapters' environment checks are bypassed in the conformance run only (cell.json dataOnly.bypassEnvironmentCheck), so the suite shows what would happen past them. Results are data, never verification: nothing here enters verifiedRanges or changes a peer range.

groups.description: The Pixi 7 adapter on pixi.js releases outside its peer range: the highest patch of 7.0 and 7.1 (below the 7.2.0 floor), and the excluded 7.4.0 (7.4.1 was never published to npm). Pixi 7.2 and 7.3, and React 18.0 to 18.2, were data-only probes until they became matrix cells (React 18 per-minor packages, the Pixi 7 range widened to 7.2).
